title: Fractions at work
goal: I can link fractions and division. I can find a fraction of a remainder, and work backwards with a bar model.

learn.intro: A fraction of a remainder is taken from what is left, not from the whole. First find what is left. Then take the fraction of that. A bar model with equal parts shows every step.

example.problem: A ribbon is 180 cm long. Mei uses 1/3 of it for a gift. Then she uses 1/4 of the ribbon that is left for a bow. How long is the ribbon that is left now?
steps: Cut the bar into 6 equal parts. Each part is 180 ÷ 6 = 30 cm. The gift uses 1/3, which is 2 parts.
The part left is 4 parts. The bow uses 1/4 of those 4 parts, which is 1 part.
The ribbon that is left is 6 - 2 - 1 = 3 parts.
example.answer: The ribbon that is left is 90 cm long.

howto.title: How to
steps: Draw a bar. Cut it into equal small parts.
Take the first fraction. Find what is left.
Take the next fraction of what is left, not of the whole.

facts.title: Remember
lines: A unit fraction has 1 on top, such as 1/5.
To add or subtract, use the same bottom number.

try.text: Mei has 120 beads. She uses 1/4 of them for a bracelet. Then she uses 2/3 of the rest for a necklace. How many beads are left? {b}
try.explanation: 1/4 of 120 = 30, so 90 beads are left. 2/3 of 90 = 60 beads for the necklace. 90 - 60 = 30 beads are left.

items.text: Fill in the blanks. Write each answer as a fraction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: 7 pizzas are shared equally among 10 children. Each child gets {b} of a pizza.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A 3 m rope is cut into 8 equal pieces. Each piece is {b} m long.

items.text: Circle the greater amount in each pair.
items.explanation: (a) 1/6 is less than 1/5 (shortfall from 1), so 5/6. (b) 35/63 and 36/63: 4/7. (c) 15 and 16: 2/3 of 24.

items.text: A bar of 8 equal parts is 64 cm long. Find the fractions of the bar.
items.explanation: 1 part is 64 ÷ 8 = 8 cm. (a) 3 parts = 24 cm. (b) 5 parts = 40 cm. (c) 1/4 is 2 parts of the 8, which is 16 cm.

items.text: Find each answer. Write it in its simplest form.
Ravi walks 3/4 km each day. He does this for 6 days. How far does he walk in all? Write a mixed number. {b} km
items.explanation: 6 × 3/4 = 18/4. Divide 18 by 4: 4 with 2 left over, so 4 and 2/4, which is 4 1/2. Or: 3/4 of 6 is 4 1/2.

items.text: Sam has 72 cards. He gives 1/3 of them to Mei. Then he gives 3/4 of the cards that are left to Ben. How many cards does Sam have now? {b}

Write 7/12 as a sum of 2 different unit fractions. A unit fraction has 1 on top.
Take away 1/3 first: 7/12 - 1/3 = {b}. So 7/12 = 1/3 + {b}.
items.explanation: 1/3 = 4/12. 7/12 - 4/12 = 3/12 = 1/4. Both 1/3 and 1/4 have 1 on top and they are different, so 7/12 = 1/3 + 1/4.

items.text: Look at the pattern: 1/3, 2/5, 3/7, 4/9, ...
items.explanation: The top is the position and the bottom is 2n + 1. (a) 5/11 and 6/13. (b) 10/21. (c) 13/27: 2 × 13 + 1 = 27, so the 13th.

items.text: Ali reads 2/5 of a book on Saturday and 1/4 of the book on Sunday. What fraction of the book is not read yet? {b}
Mark Mei's points A and B on the number line. Write each as a mixed number.

figure.alt: number line from 0 to 2 in quarters

items.explanation: Each mark is 1/4. A is 1 and 1 quarter: 1 1/4. B is 1 3/4.

items.text: Multiply. Write each answer in its simplest form.
items.explanation: Multiply the tops and the bottoms, then simplify. (a) 6/24 = 1/4. (b) 6/15 = 2/5. (c) 12/9 = 4/3 = 1 1/3.

items.text: Mei buys a book with 1/3 of her money. Then she pays 1/2 of the rest for lunch. She has $18 left. Use the model.
items.explanation: The book is 1 part, lunch is 1 part and the $18 left is 1 part. So 3 parts = $54.

items.text: In a group of 40 children, 3/8 walk to school and 1/4 take the bus. The rest cycle. How many children cycle? {b}
items.explanation: 3/8 of 40 = 15 walk. 1/4 of 40 = 10 take the bus. 15 + 10 = 25, so 40 - 25 = 15 cycle.

items.text: Circle True or False.
Write 2/5 as the sum of 2 different unit fractions. Try 1/3 first, then 1/4, then 1/5. Stop when the first fraction is less than half of 2/5.
items.hint: Take away a unit fraction. Is what is left a unit fraction?
items.explanation: 2/5 - 1/3 = 1/15, so 2/5 = 1/3 + 1/15. 2/5 - 1/4 = 3/20 is not a unit fraction. 1/5 is half of 2/5, so stop. Only this way.

items.text: A shop sells 1/3 of its eggs in the morning. It sells 1/4 of the rest in the afternoon. In the evening it sells 2/5 of the eggs then left. At the end 36 eggs are left. How many eggs did the shop have at first? {b}
items.hint: Find the fraction of ALL the eggs that is left at each step.
items.explanation: After the morning 2/3 are left. Then 3/4 of 2/3 = 1/2. Then 3/5 of 1/2 = 3/10. 36 is 3/10, so 1/10 is 12 and the whole is 120.

items.text: Look at the cards. Make 2 fractions and add them. Each card is used once. The fractions need not be proper.
items.hint: A big top and a small bottom make a big fraction.
items.explanation: Greatest: big top, small bottom: 7/2 + 5/3 = 31/6 = 5 1/6. Smallest: small tops, big bottoms: 2/5 + 3/7 = 29/35.

items.text: 5/6 of a cake is shared equally among 10 children. What fraction of the whole cake does each child get? {b}
items.hint: Cut each sixth into 2 equal parts. How many parts are there?
items.explanation: Cut every sixth into 2 equal parts. Then 5/6 becomes 10 parts, and each part is 1/12 of the cake. So 5/6 ÷ 10 = 1/12.

items.text: Write 1/6 as the sum of 2 different unit fractions. How many ways are there? {b} ways
items.hint: Test 1/7, 1/8, 1/9 ... Stop when the first is under half of 1/6.
items.explanation: Test 1/7, 1/8, 1/9 and 1/10: each leaves a unit fraction (1/42, 1/24, 1/18, 1/15). 1/11 leaves 5/66: no. 1/12 is half of 1/6, so stop. 4 ways.

items.text: A ball falls from a height. Each time it bounces up to 3/4 of the height it fell from. After the 3rd bounce it reaches 27 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The ball fell from {b} cm at first.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The first bounce that is under half the first height is bounce {b}.

items.hint: After 3 bounces the height is 3/4 of 3/4 of 3/4 of the start.
items.explanation: Work backwards: 27 ÷ 3/4 = 36, 36 ÷ 3/4 = 48, 48 ÷ 3/4 = 64. Heights 64, 48, 36, 27. Half of 64 is 32, so 27 is the first under it: bounce 3.
Write each as 1/2 × (a difference). The middle parts cancel, leaving 1/2 × (1 - 1/9) = 4/9.

items.text: 5 pizzas are shared equally among 6 children. Write the answers as fractions.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Each child gets {b} of a pizza.

items.explanation: (a) 5 ÷ 6 = 5/6. (b) 7 ÷ 3: 3 goes into 7 two times with 1 left, so 2 and 1/3.
